A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP generalization study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled CLIP and supervised-classifier experiments, together with feature-sharing, representational-similarity, and circuit analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds BLIP experiments and evaluations using additional metrics.

M1.justification: The CLIP training procedure and SAE, CKA, and circuit-analysis methods are retained. Algorithms 1–2 document the existing feature-sharing calculation more explicitly; BLIP is added as an evaluated alternative.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-Captions, CC3M, CC12M, DomainNet, and ImageNet-Sketch for the same domain and compositional generalization scenarios. The added BLIP experiments use the existing Clipart and Sketch coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds BLIP to the evaluated comparison methods in Appendix B.1, Table 10, and Figure 12. The existing CLIP architecture variants, SigLIP, and supervised-classifier comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds balanced top-5 accuracy and macro F1 evaluation, plus a BLIP experiment using an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B-16 and BERT-base initialization. Appendix B.3 also revises the interpolation description to specify training samples; this wording change does not establish that the existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds checks of whether the findings persist across alternative metrics and BLIP pre-training. Appendix C.3 newly reports checking that circuits are distinguishable at the initial Weisfeiler-Lehman iteration. The domain-addition, class-overlap, interpolation, and existing mechanistic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Figure 2 captions specify averaging over three consecutive epochs and three seeds. The three-run reporting and existing uncertainty values in Table 6 and the supervised-results table are unchanged; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables retain their numerical results. v2 adds alternative-metric curves and BLIP results, including 55.6% Clipart and 61.2% Sketch accuracy under CG high-diversity in Table 10; these are additional results under different model conditions. The carbon estimate changes from approximately 2,600 to 1,725 kgCO2eq using a different electricity-emissions factor.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 and Equations (1)–(12) retain their mathematical content. The added SAE pseudocode details an existing calculation, while the Weisfeiler-Lehman discussion qualifies limitations without introducing a new formal result, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: domain diversity supports generalization, compositional generalization can underperform domain generalization, and successful generalization requires sufficient feature and circuit sharing. Added validation does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a hypothesis that shared contour features explain diminishing benefits from combining Sketch and Quickdraw. Section 7 expands discussion of dataset size and quality, and Appendix C.3 adds limitations and mitigating factors concerning Weisfeiler-Lehman false positives. The principal interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised future code release with a stated repository link. It documents SAE feature selection and aggregation through Algorithms 1–2, specifies the BLIP initialization and LAVIS implementation, identifies nnsight, and clarifies that Leave-out-domain also participates in dataset-size matching. These are chiefly added disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds prior CLIP domain-generalization approaches by Huang, Bose, Addepalli, and Yu and colleagues. Additional references support BLIP, LAVIS, its encoders, and interpretability tools. The overall research positioning remains stable; publication-year updates to existing cited works are not new references.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations of domain interactions and feature/circuit analysis, organizes circuit analysis into explicit steps, harmonizes class notation, and moves class-mapping details from Appendix A.7 to A.3. The overall section sequence and most of the narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 combines v1 Figures 3 and 8 into a two-panel Figure 3, moves Figure 1 earlier, and adds the alternative-metric figure and BLIP table/plots. Captions, legends, plot sizes, and float placement receive limited revisions; most existing displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional validation through alternative metrics and BLIP, improves documentation of the SAE analysis, supplies a stated code location, and explains more limitations. These strengthen reproducibility and interpretation while retaining the original evidence. BLIP's different architecture and pretrained initialization limit conclusions from its higher scores, so the gains support a modest overall improvement.
